note: Adapted from the original English description of Snyder 1929. Reason for establishing the species: Hagen 1858 named Calotermes posticus from a dealate female from St. Thomas, and Banks 1919 then treated a soldier from Jamaica as the soldier of that species, noting "if not, then it is a new species"; Snyder considered the identity of posticus highly doubtful and probably a Cryptotermes (perhaps C. cavifrons), and therefore established the new name liberatus for the Jamaican specimen recorded by Banks, type locality Cinchona, Jamaica, the type soldier in the American Museum of Natural History. The original describes the soldier only; the alate and the worker are unknown. The key in the same paper separates it from bequaerti (both with a transparent eye spot and a slender postmentum) by the finely serrate anterior margin of the pronotum in bequaerti, which this species lacks.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head yellow; mandibles reddish brown with black tips; pronotum pale brown; body dull yellow; legs and antennae pale. Head about twice as long as wide, the sides parallel and hardly convex, broadly rounded behind, steeply declining in front; clypeus nearly square. Mandibles shorter than the head width, stout, with the usual dentition. Antennae short, hardly longer than the head width, the third segment not modified. Eye spots not visible. Pronotum more than twice as wide as long, the anterior margin concave, the posterior margin slightly convex, the sides rounded, hardly narrowed posteriorly. Head and body with sparse, moderately long erect hairs; legs short, the hind femora much swollen. Head length 3 mm.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The key appended to the same paper places this species alongside K. (K.) bequaerti, K. (K.) banksi, K. (K.) schwarzi and K. (K.) joueli: only liberatus and bequaerti have a transparent eye spot and a slender postmentum, and bequaerti has the anterior margin of the pronotum finely serrate, whereas this species does not.
